about: Piece 7: the named correlations of the convective heat-transfer examples, each with its constants, source, the measured data behind it and its validity range; the empirical boundaries with their cited values and bands; the published reference values; and the definitions that an imported numerical-results file must use. The page evaluates a correlation only inside its range.

correlations.name: Pohlhausen's laminar flat-plate correlation, local
correlations.data: A power-law fit to Pohlhausen's exact similarity solution of the laminar boundary-layer equations: within 2 % for Pr ≥ 0.6 and within 1 % for 0.6 ≤ Pr ≤ 2. The upper limit of Re_x is the start of transition in a laboratory wind tunnel.

correlations.name: Laminar flat-plate correlation, mean over the length
correlations.data: The integral of eqn. (6.58) over the plate: h̄ = 2h(x = L). It holds when the whole plate is laminar.

correlations.name: Turbulent flat-plate correlation of Reynolds et al., local, gases
correlations.data: Measurements of Reynolds et al. for air over a constant-temperature plate; for gases only. The page takes 0.6 ≤ Pr ≤ 1 as the range of gases, and Re_x ≥ 4 × 10⁶ where the layer is fully turbulent in every case.

correlations.name: Gnielinski's correlation for turbulent tube flow
correlations.data: Gnielinski's fit to a large set of measured data: more than 90 % of the liquid data within ±20 %, and better for gases. For a uniform wall temperature or heat flux.

correlations.name: Churchill and Chu, laminar vertical wall
correlations.data: Churchill and Chu fitted the Squire–Eckert form to measured data of 13 independent studies with many fluids. For laminar natural convection, Ra_L < 10⁹, a uniform wall temperature or heat flux, and properties at the film temperature.

correlations.name: Churchill and Chu, vertical wall, all Ra_L
correlations.data: The same data, including the turbulent layer above Ra_L = 10⁹. Lienhard states that it can be used for all Ra_L and Pr; eqn. (8.13a) is more accurate in the laminar range.

plate.data: Laminar flow can begin to break down at Re_x ≈ 30 000 in a highly disturbed flow. In a laboratory wind tunnel transition often starts between 2 × 10⁵ and 5 × 10⁵. Very careful experiments delayed the onset to 2.8 × 10⁶ and fully turbulent flow to 4 × 10⁶.

regions.label: Laminar unless the stream is highly disturbed
Transition range: laminar or turbulent, by the stream and the surface

tube.data: The minimum transitional Reynolds number is about 2100; Gnielinski's correlation holds from Re_D = 2300 to 5 × 10⁶.

regions.label: Near the minimum transitional Re_D: no declared result
Above the range of the correlation

entry.data: x_et/D ≈ 0.034 Re_D Pr for a uniform wall temperature and 0.043 Re_D Pr for a uniform wall heat flux; beyond x_et the Nusselt number is within 5 % of the fully developed value.

regions.label: Thermal entry region: the local Nu is above the fully developed value by more than 5 %

wall.data: The boundary layer becomes turbulent at Rayleigh numbers above about 10⁹; eqn. (8.13a) lies on the low side of the data there. Eqn. (8.13b) holds for all Ra_L.

plate-convection.describe: Each point gives the local Nu_x/Re_x^(1/2) of a laminar layer on an isothermal plate at one Prandtl number. The page compares it with 0.332 Pr^(1/3) where Pr ≥ 0.6; the stated agreement of the correlation is 2 %.
